chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man upon whom doubt fell, and he did not know whether he prostrated once or twice, he (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him prostrate one more.'

key_terms.شُبِّهَ عَلَيْهِ: Doubt fell upon him / He was in doubt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one doubts the number of prostrations in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *Sajdat al-Shakk* (prostration of doubt) for uncertainty in the number of prostrations, specifically when the doubt arises between one and two. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach of relying on the 'most likely' count while using the extra prostration to rectify the potential deficiency, ensuring the validity of the prayer without requiring a full re-performance.
